blocks.x: Applied AI & GenAI applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Energy & Utilities, applied ai & generative ai at dataq soft covers the full lifecycle of enterprise intelligence: strategy and value mapping, platform build-out, model adaptation, retrieval architectures, multimodal systems, and the governance fabric that keeps every model auditable. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise ai strategy & roadmapping, generative ai platform engineering, llm fine-tuning & model operations — delivered on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Renewable supply and flexible demand make legacy forecasting blind; imbalance costs and curtailment climb while forecasts run on yesterday's methods.
IT/OT convergence, remote access growth and legacy SCADA estates create attack paths with physical consequences; CIP/NIS2 duties expand faster than programs mature.
Turbines, transformers and pipelines hold decades of life left — and zero telemetry. Condition-based maintenance is impossible without sensing, and failures cost the most when they are unscheduled.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Applied AI & Generative AI tower — Enterprise AI Strategy & Roadmapping, Generative AI Platform Engineering, LLM Fine-Tuning & Model Operations, RAG & Enterprise Knowledge Systems as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: CSRD / ISSB obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Align AI to P&L lines and risk mandates — a sequenced portfolio, not a pile of pilots.
One governed platform, many GenAI products: retrieval, guardrails and cost control as shared services.
Own your models: tune, distill and operate LLMs with measurable quality, controlled cost and enforceable policy.
Answers with citations, not vibes: permission-aware retrieval over your regulated document estate.
Weather-coupled ML ensembles at asset and portfolio level feeding trading (imbalance cost down via better forecasts)
Market context summarized with citations to exchange data and risk policy (trader coverage widened per desk)
Unplanned outage hours on critical assets

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: CSRD / ISSB and NERC CIP (North America). Critical-infrastructure protection standards for bulk power systems. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
